incident: Emotet Strikes Again - LNK to domain-wide Quantum ransomware (8 days)

sources.title: Emotet Strikes Again - LNK File Leads to Domain Wide Ransomware - The DFIR Report (2022-11-28)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (malspam LNK -> PowerShell -> Emotet via regsvr32), hops (CS beacon to a workstation via SMB+WMI, SMB+remote services across DCs and servers, Tactical RMM/AnyDesk, RDP incl backup server), cred access (LSASS Mimikatz, suspected Zerologon), exfil (Rclone to Mega ~250MB), impact (Quantum domain-wide over SMB), 154h

narrative_before: In a June 2022 intrusion the DFIR Report observed a user double-click a malspam LNK that ran encoded PowerShell to download an Emotet DLL (run via regsvr32, Registry Run Key persistence) on the beachhead host. Emotet ran daily discovery and spammed. On day 3 Emotet dropped a Cobalt Strike beacon; the actors moved laterally to a workstation (SMB transfer + WMI execution), dumped LSASS there, enumerated SMB shares and reviewed documents on a file server. On day 4 they used SMB file transfers and remote services to move across domain controllers and several servers with CS beacon DLLs (find.bat/p.bat AdFind + ping sweep on the DC); a suspected Zerologon attempt was seen from the beachhead to a DC. On another server they deployed Tactical RMM and used Rclone to exfiltrate ~250MB from a file share to Mega. On day 8 they used Tactical RMM to deploy AnyDesk, ran SoftPerfect Network Scanner, RDPed to other hosts including a backup server, dropped Powertool64.exe/dontsleep.exe, then locker.dll + 1.bat to deploy Quantum ransomware to all hosts over SMB. Time to ransomware was 154 hours over 8 days.

detection_moments.description: Emotet running on the beachhead (LNK/PowerShell/regsvr32) with daily discovery; day 3 Cobalt Strike beacon dropped.
detection_moments.evidence: 'a user double clicked a LNK file, which then executed encoded Powershell commands to download an Emotet DLL ... Emotet dropped a Cobalt Strike executable beacon onto the beachhead host' - Emotet Strikes Again, The DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: Day 3-4: CS beacon to a workstation via SMB+WMI, LSASS dumped there; SMB+remote service movement across DCs and servers; suspected Zerologon from beachhead to a DC; file server documents reviewed.
detection_moments.evidence: 'transfer a beacon executable over SMB ... executed via WMI ... dump credentials from the LSASS process ... a flight of netlogon authentications ... as a possible attempt at exploiting the domain controller' - Emotet Strikes Again

detection_moments.description: Tactical RMM deployed on a server; Rclone exfiltrates ~250MB from a file share to Mega.
detection_moments.evidence: 'the threat actors deployed Tactical RMM ... using Rclone to exfiltrate data from a file share server ... The Mega.io service ... at least ~250MB' - Emotet Strikes Again

detection_moments.description: Day 8: AnyDesk via Tactical RMM, netscan, RDP to hosts incl backup server; locker.dll + 1.bat deploy Quantum to all hosts over SMB.
detection_moments.evidence: 'locker.dll and a batch file 1.bat were dropped on the host and the batch file was executed beginning the Quantum ransomware deployment to all hosts over SMB' - Emotet Strikes Again

attack_path: malspam LNK runs encoded PowerShell downloading Emotet via regsvr32 (T1566.001/T1204.002)
Cobalt Strike beacon copied over SMB and executed via WMI; LSASS dumped (T1021.002/T1047/T1003.001)
SMB + remote service CS DLLs across domain controllers (T1021.002)
Rclone exfiltration of a file share to Mega from a Tactical RMM server (T1567.002)
RDP to backup server and other hosts before Quantum deployment over SMB (T1021.001/T1486)
ambiguities: Hosts named by role only; victim sector not stated.
Zerologon only suspected (failed/attempt); domain admin acquisition not explicitly confirmed.
Exact set of 'several other servers' not enumerated; modelled as srv_1/srv_2.
Moments are the report's own daily timeline markers, not a defender detection timeline.
